description.short_caption: Cryptosporidium organisms on H&E stain of gallbladder epithelium (arrows).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of gallbladder tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The epithelial lining is visible, with small, round to oval basophilic structures (indicated by arrows) attached to the epithelial surface. These structures are consistent with Cryptosporidium organisms. The surrounding tissue shows mild inflammatory changes.
visible_findings: small basophilic round to oval structures attached to epithelium (arrows)
mild inflammatory changes in surrounding tissue

Case_09015/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Histopathological examination of the gallbladder with H and E stain.

description.short_caption: Histopathological examination of the gallbladder with H&E stain showing epithelial and inflammatory changes.
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image shows a section of gallbladder tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The epithelium appears hyperplastic with tall columnar cells and basally located nuclei. There is evidence of inflammatory infiltrates in the lamina propria, consisting predominantly of lymphocytes. The architecture suggests chronic inflammation, possibly consistent with chronic cholecystitis. The staining highlights cellular and tissue details effectively.
visible_findings: hyperplastic epithelium with tall columnar cells
inflammatory infiltrates in the lamina propria

Case_09015/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Histopathological examination of the gallbladder with H and E stain.

description.short_caption: Histopathological examination of the gallbladder with H&E stain showing epithelial and inflammatory changes.
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image shows a section of gallbladder tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The epithelium appears hyperplastic with some areas of irregular architecture. There is a notable presence of inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and plasma cells, within the lamina propria. The staining highlights cellular and nuclear details, aiding in the identification of pathological changes.
visible_findings: H&E staining with clear nuclear and cytoplasmic detail
